key_insight: RAPID shows that a robot can learn a usable program from a single human demonstration by treating robot task learning like an agentic coding problem. It automatically generates, tests, and refines code until the behavior matches the demonstration.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of turning a one-time visual human demonstration into a reliable robot program without requiring extensive manual programming, hand-crafted task logic, or large training datasets.
method: Start from a single visual demonstration and convert it into an initial robot program.
Use an iterative agentic loop to generate, execute, verify, and refine code based on task tests.
Leverage action primitives and a testable task specification so the system can check whether the program matches the demonstrated behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, RAPID suggests a practical path toward faster robot skill acquisition with less human supervision. It bridges coding agents and robotics, making robot programming more scalable and easier to adapt to new tasks.
